_comment: TEMPLATE, not a device. Copy it to devices/<slug>.json (no leading underscore) and replace everything. Made-up product ids: 900 is 'your' device, 901 its sibling.

server.mjs loads every devices/*.json except files starting with '_' (like this one), merges them and hot-reloads each file on its own. A broken file is logged, listed under 'errors' in /__mirror/status, and its previous version stays active.
Check a file without starting anything: node server.mjs --check (all device files) or node server.mjs --check --rules devices/<slug>.json (one file).
Every key that starts with '_' is ignored by the server. In this template, '_<key>' explains the key next to it. The working example is devices/basilisk-v3.json.
Regexes are JavaScript regex source strings: escape backslashes for JSON (\. for a literal dot, \d for a digit).

device._device: Who this file is for. lib.sh (mirror_check, used by launch.sh, agent.sh and status.sh) waits until /synapse/dashboard/AvailableDevices.json lists device.productId of every device file.
device.name: Razer Example Mouse
device._name: Display name, for status output and the README. The name Synapse shows comes from the module (rewrite it there).
device._productId: Required. The USB product id IN DECIMAL (ioreg idProduct; 0x0099 = 153). Synapse's device lists and the /synapse/products/<pid>/ paths use this number.
device._cloneOf: The sibling whose published Mac module this device borrows. Informational; the routes below do the work. Pick a sibling with the same body, buttons and connection type: a wired device must not clone a wireless one.
device._backend: The active backend name for this file (default '203-mac'). Entries with a 'backend' field apply only while it is active. MIRROR_BACKEND / --backend NAME switches every device file that has a backend called NAME; the others keep their own.
device._verified: Date of the live test on real hardware, or null while unverified.
notes: What works, what the firmware rejects (with the products_<pid>_mw log line), what is not verified.
device._notes: Free text, shown nowhere by the server. Keep the honest list of known gaps here.

_upstreamHost: Optional, global: the default upstream host. Every file that sets it must agree; the first file wins and a conflict is reported as an error.
_resolve: Optional, global: pin an upstream IP instead of DNS, {"apps-mac.razer.com": ["<real ip>"]}. Loopback is always refused. Leave empty.

jsonEdits._jsonEdit: Structural edit of a JSON response. All jsonEdits whose 'match' fits the request path are applied in file order, so several device files can each add their own entry to the same dashboard list.
jsonEdits.name: dashboard-available-add-900
jsonEdits._match: Required. Regex on the request path; the query string (?d=, ?_= cache-busters) is not part of it.
jsonEdits._key: Identity field of array entries (default productId).
jsonEdits._ensure: Array roots: each entry is appended when no entry has the same key value. For a wireless device copy dongleId/bleId from Razer's own entry in UnavailableDevices.json. Do not add repId: the sibling module never reads realProductId.
jsonEdits._why: Free text: why this edit exists.

jsonEdits.name: dashboard-lists-drop-900
jsonEdits._remove: Array roots: entries whose key value is listed are dropped. A list with nothing to drop is served byte-identical.

jsonEdits.name: installer-manifest-add-osx
jsonEdits._backend: Optional: a backend name or an array of names; omit for every backend. This edit only runs while the backend 900-win is active.
jsonEdits._setIfMissing: Object roots: dotted path -> value, written only when the path does not exist.
jsonEdits._set: Object roots: dotted path -> value, always written, e.g. {"a.b": 1}. Empty here.

routes._route: Routes are tried in order across all device files; the first whose backend is active and whose 'match' fits wins. Only match your own /synapse/products/<pid>/ paths, so loading every device file stays harmless. A response a route or jsonEdit touches is 'managed': fetched uncompressed and in full, edited, sent with Cache-Control no-store.
routes.name: lighting-manifest-900
routes._why: Serve Razer's genuine lighting manifest for this pid when it exists upstream. Must come before the generic module route.

routes.name: module-900-from-901
routes._name: Shown in logs (route:<name>), the X-Mirror-Route header and /__mirror/status.
routes._backend: Optional: string, array, or omitted (every backend).
routes._match: Required. Regex on the request path (no query string).
routes._host: Optional upstream host for this route (default upstreamHost). The Windows module of a pid lives on apps.razer.com.
routes._path: Optional String.replace template applied to the request path with 'match' ($1, $<name>). Omit to keep the path.

pathRewrite.name: 900_-segments-to-901_
pathRewrite._why: Rewrite entries (same format as 'rewrite' below) applied to the mapped upstream path. Here: path segments named after the pid, such as /900_0/PluginImages/900_0_0_dashboard3x.avif.

routes._pathRewrite: Optional list of rewrite entries for the upstream path.
routes._keepQuery: Append the original query string upstream (default true).
routes._noStore: Send Cache-Control no-store and drop ETag/Last-Modified (default true).
routes._textTypes: Regex on Content-Type: which bodies are edited. Default: js, html, json, css, plain; an octet-stream body falls back to its file extension.
routes._noRewrite: Regex on the request path: body rewrites are skipped and the body is served byte-identical (jsonEdits still apply). Signed manifests belong here.

rewrite.name: productId
rewrite._name: Shown in warn= lines and recentWarnings.
rewrite._literal: Exact text to replace (every occurrence). Use either 'literal' or 'pattern'.
rewrite._replace: Replacement. With 'pattern' it has String.replace semantics ($1, $<name>, $&).
rewrite._required: Optional regex on the request path: a 2xx response there with 0 matches is refused with 502 instead of being served unpatched. Use it for the productId gate in the main bundles.
rewrite._expect: Optional: upstream path suffix -> match count of today's build. A different count is logged as warn= and listed under recentWarnings; the file is still served. Keys name hashed files, so a renamed bundle gives no warning (that is what 'required' is for).

rewrite.name: translation-keys
rewrite._paths: Optional regex on the request path that limits this entry to some files.
rewrite._flags: Regex flags for 'pattern'; 'g' is always added.

routes._rewrite: Body rewrites, run in order on 2xx textual bodies (UTF-8, or latin1 when the body is not UTF-8) unless 'noRewrite' matches. Typical set for a clone: productId (required), webpack context keys "./901_, translation keys "901_N":, service-worker precache URLs, product names in every language, maxDPI and the DPI slider, master-guide and support-page ids.

routes.name: module-900-from-windows
routes._why: Alternative backend: Razer's Windows module for the same pid, no rewrites. Untested for any device; it needs the osx installer block above. See README, Add your own device.
